title: Nits from vc's reads of ISSUE:0008's two units and ic's read of its landed text, for a later release
body:
## Context

vc's two reads of cc's ISSUE:0008 units on 2026-11-17 passed both to land in 0.1.10. These six findings were left for a later release, since hv wants one cut and no small releases (decision 2). None blocks a switch or loses a login.

ic's read of ISSUE:0008's landed user-facing text in 0.1.10's source (5d8346a), sent to cc on 2026-11-17 at 07:25Z, added items 7 to 11, in ic's wording. On vc's word of 2026-11-17 they are fixed in the same unit as items 1 to 6, so the next release's text changes are one run. Items 3 and 5 are ruled out, each with its reason below.

## Items

1. `src/usage.rs`, about lines 840 to 843: a renewed login that turns out to be another account's gets the generic "could not verify the renewed login matches this profile", with no remedy. It predates ISSUE:0008 and needs a narrow race.
2. `sessions::pinned_to` compares paths as written, so a session pinned through a symlink or a relative path is not seen by doctor or by the refusal. A pin normally comes from `ccusage dir`, which prints an absolute path. Found by cc in the build, reading Claude Code 2.1.326's own code: Claude Code names a login's Keychain item from the variable's value as written, in its NFC form, and resolves nothing. So on macOS a pin through a symlink or a relative path names another item and is rightly not seen; a pin spelt in another Unicode form names the same item and is missed; and a pin with a trailing slash names another item yet is matched, since a path comparison ignores the slash. Elsewhere Claude Code reads the credentials file, which the filesystem reaches through a symlink, and from the session's working directory when the path is relative, so there both are missed. The fix keeps the path comparison and adds to it the store each directory gives Claude Code, found as Claude Code finds it on that platform, so a match is never narrower than before: another Unicode spelling now matches on macOS, and a symlink or a relative path elsewhere, for the refusal, doctor's pinned sessions and WARN, and the pinned count alike. A trailing slash stays matched on macOS, since narrowing a match could miss a pin, while a wrong match only refuses a move.
3. `switch::admitted` calls `usage::verified_token`, so an incoming profile with an email and an expiring token is renewed in its own store before the check refuses it as Foreign: refused before any move, but not before every write. The outgoing check behaves the same way. Ruled out: `auth::fresh` renews only a token that is expired or about to expire, and the profile endpoint cannot check an expired one, so the check needs the renewal. The renewal writes the same login back into the same store, under Claude Code's lock protocol, as Claude Code itself does at any time: no login moves, no account gains or loses one, and the refusal still comes before any move, journal or selection. Refusing an expiring login unrenewed would refuse most switches to an idle account. The outgoing check is the same. `verified_token`'s doc says so.
4. A seated profile with no email and no account record is always refused, and the Foreign message says "run ccusage login NAME", which repeats the refusal. It should point to setting the profile's email.
5. `sessions_note` in `src/cli.rs` and `pinned_now` in `src/display.rs` drop a `shared_dir()` error (`if let Ok`, `.ok()`), so a config error makes the pinned note disappear without a word, though the verb's main path reports the error (No Silent Errors). Ruled out: a `shared_dir()` error is the same error every account's report carries on that run, since `seat::home` reads `shared_dir()` first: which gives it as each account's reason, predict in each left-out line, usage and the TUI on each account's row. With no shared config there is nothing to count the sessions against, so the note says nothing, as `shell_note`'s doc already says for its own case. The docs of `sessions_note` and `pinned_now` say so.
6. `relocate`'s retry on Foreign verifies both logins again, so a foreign incoming login costs two profile calls before its refusal. Cost only.
7. One term for a session a switch leaves behind (ISSUE:0008's item 6). `src/sessions.rs:245` and `249` say "N running Claude sessions are pinned to logins other than the shared config's, so a switch does not move them; ccusage doctor names them". Every other line the user reads says "reads" and "does not follow a switch": doctor's WARN (`src/doctor.rs:359`), `shell_pin`, and remedy and refusal ("Claude session N reads NAME's own store"). No other user-facing line says "pinned". Suggest: "N running Claude sessions read a login other than the shared config's, so they do not follow a switch; ccusage doctor names them", and for one session: "1 running Claude session reads a login other than the shared config's, so it does not follow a switch; ccusage doctor names it". README and the CHANGELOG say "how many running sessions a switch does not move"; that can follow or stay.
8. Three lines where a word can point two ways.
   - (a) `src/doctor.rs:129`, the FAIL for two logins, ends "{remedy}, which leaves it one login". After a remedy that names a session ("... restart it from a shell without ..., and only then run ccusage login NAME"), "it" can read as the session. Suggest "which leaves NAME one login".
   - (b) `src/doctor.rs:359`, the drift WARN: "restart it from a shell without it", where the second "it" is the variable. This line is older (2ad2745), but the new remedies sit beside it. Suggest "restart it from a shell without VAR (unset VAR)", where VAR is the variable its cause names.
   - (c) `src/sessions.rs:217`, the remedy when the sessions cannot be listed: "first restart any started with CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR naming NAME's own store from a shell without it". Here "from a shell without it" can attach to "started". Suggest "first restart, from a shell without CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR (unset CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR), any Claude session started with it naming NAME's own store, and only then run ccusage login NAME". That also gives this case the "(unset ...)" that the pinned case and the refusal give.
9. predict's left-out lines (`src/predict/view.rs:61`, with `src/predict.rs:300`). "NAME: left out, the rate leaves out its 12 weekly samples, ..." says "left out" twice. An account on another plan also names its plan twice: "c: left out, another plan's allowance (Pro); the rate leaves out its 12 weekly samples, on Pro". Suggest, for that case: "c: left out, another plan's allowance (Pro), with its 12 weekly samples".
10. A projected account with any weekly sample taken on another plan also goes into left_out. `src/predict.rs:433` to `441` pushes every account with samples left out that is not in left_out yet, and nothing checks whether it is projected. Take an account now on the counted plan with older samples on another plan: an upgrade does this, and so does a rate_limit_tier string that changes, which would touch every account at once. predict then prints both "x: 40% used now, ..." and "x: left out, the rate leaves out 3 of its 60 weekly samples, on Pro", and predict --json names x in both accounts and left_out. README's version 1 says left_out is "each account left out as {name, reason}". Nothing in hv's estate shows this today, and the Herdr panel does not read left_out. The meaning is cc's and the shape is ic's. Decided by cc, with vc's view, on 2026-11-17: left_out holds only the accounts that are not projected, as version 1 says; a projected account's left-out samples get a text line of their own, without "left out,"; and no JSON field is added unless a reader needs one now.
11. The fall line (ISSUE:0008's item 7), `src/predict/view.rs:76`. Three full UTC stamps make it the longest line predict prints, and predict's other lines give durations ("at its reset in 3d04h"). Suggest durations for the two samples and the window, eg "NAME: weekly usage fell from 40% 3h10 ago to 12% 1h05 ago, in the window that resets in 3d04h, as the usage endpoint reported it; the rate counts a fall as no use".

## Acceptance

- Each item is fixed, with a test where it changes behaviour, or ruled out with its reason in this record.




## Progress

- 2026-11-17: landed on main on vc's read of the diff. cc's unit, replayed by vc onto ic's ISSUE:0012 (4930094): 2e38bee (the tests), ae1cc8a (the fix), f6788cd (the AT rows). cc's run, Desk slot 01M7M6NNYD91SFXPA7W3HCCMRX: red at 3948105, the 13 new or changed tests failing as meant; green at 0ce2f13 (build, test rust with 111 lib and 59 cli passed, check format and clippy). The landed src, tests and Cargo files are identical to 0ce2f13.
- The follow-up, 31935d5, replayed from cc's b602cd1: three tests derive the counts they expect from their fixtures, under hv's rule against hand-written counts in tests, and the CHANGELOG's Changed line reads "and so do not follow a switch", from ic's read. cc's run, Desk slot 01M7M8R6G5CAFC14K56GD2Y3H4: test rust (111 lib, 59 cli), check format and clippy.
- Fixed, each with its test: item 1, a_renewed_login_of_another_account_is_refused_as_a_mismatch (src/usage.rs); item 2, a_directory_names_a_store_as_claude_code_reaches_it (src/sessions.rs), whose Linux branch first compiles in dc's kovacs gates before the next cut; item 4, a_login_of_a_seated_profile_with_nothing_to_check_it_against_is_refused_first (tests/cli.rs); item 6, a_move_is_tried_again_only_when_a_verified_login_changed_under_it (src/switch.rs).
- Ruled out, with the reasons above: items 3 and 5, with doc lines on verified_token, sessions_note and pinned_now.
- Items 7 to 11, in ic's signed wording: 7, the_count_of_sessions_that_do_not_follow_a_switch_is_worded_as_doctor_words_them and the CLI test which_and_predict_say_how_many_running_sessions_a_switch_does_not_move; 8(a), in doctor's where_logins_are test; 8(b), a_session_that_does_not_follow_a_switch_is_told_which_variable_to_unset; 8(c), in the sessions remedy test; 9 and 10, samples_the_rate_leaves_out_never_leave_a_projected_account_out and the left-out tests beside it; 11, the falls test, in durations for a window that has reset and for one that has not.
- Citations: the 20 rows the unit moved were re-cited at a07ed78 and checked line by line by cc's own script. intent at lint on main said ST0002 28 of 28 and ST0003 32 of 32, but on a Completed thread it skips the cited-line check (Intent issue 0665; issue 0698 makes it say so, found by intent-vc from cc's finding). intent doctor --scope all on main at 4740312, which does check a closed thread's citations, reports no closed-contract-drift.
- Ships in the next release, under the CHANGELOG's 0.1.11, unreleased.
